definitions.rationale: This rule expands the macro syntax solutionProgram into the exact translated Module term, so it defines a named proof term rather than adding an execution rule or mathematical fact.
definitions.text:
rule solutionProgram =>
    Module(
      FuncDef("any_int", Params("x", "y", "z"),
        Return(
          BoolOp(
            "and",
            Compare(Call(Name("type"), Name("x")), CmpOp("==", Name("int"))),
            Compare(Call(Name("type"), Name("y")), CmpOp("==", Name("int"))),
            Compare(Call(Name("type"), Name("z")), CmpOp("==", Name("int"))),
            BoolOp(
              "or",
              Compare(BinOp("+", Name("x"), Name("y")), CmpOp("==", Name("z"))),
              Compare(BinOp("+", Name("x"), Name("z")), CmpOp("==", Name("y"))),
              Compare(BinOp("+", Name("y"), Name("z")), CmpOp("==", Name("x"))))))))

definitions.rationale: This rule expands the macro syntax RunAnyInt into Invoke applied to solutionProgram and its three arguments, making it a structural proof wrapper definition.
definitions.text: rule RunAnyInt(X, Y, Z) => Invoke(solutionProgram, X, Y, Z)
